Howl, you ships of Tarshish!” (web:Isa.23.1). The imperative cry הֵילִ֣ילוּ אֳנִיּ֣וֹת תַּרְשִׁ֗ישׁ (oshb:Isa.23.1, byte tier) is matched at the accent-stripped tier — consonants and vowel points identical, cantillation differs — by הֵילִ֖ילוּ אֳנִיּ֣וֹת תַּרְשִׁ֑ישׁ (oshb:Isa.23.14, byte tier for its own verse), rendered “Howl, you ships of Tarshish, for your stronghold is laid waste!” (web:Isa.23.14): a refrain bracket closing this row’s span by inclusio with its own opening cry. Internally the oracle serially addresses Tarshish’s ships, Sidon, and the coastland without a further vocative strong enough to argue a finer tier-1 cut; the divine-agency disclosure at web:Isa.23.9 and the quoted divine speech opened by וַיֹּ֕אמֶר (oshb:Isa.23.12, byte tier; a K/Q-bearing verse, ketiv/qere disclosed below) at web:Isa.23.12 continue the same sustained taunt rather than opening a new addressee.
